\chapter{Complexity --- Three SAT To Coloring}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.NPReductions.ThreeSATToColoring
\section{Overview}

This module formalises the classical polynomial-time reduction from 3-SAT to
3-Coloring.  Given a 3-SAT instance over Boolean variables, a gadget graph is
constructed whose vertices are palette nodes, literal nodes, and six-node clause
gadgets; the main result (\lean{SATtoColor.SATtoColorReduction}) states that the
formula is satisfiable if and only if the reduction graph admits a proper
3-coloring.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Clause]
\lean{SATtoColor.Clause}
\leanok
A \emph{clause} over a variable type $V$ is a structure bundling exactly three
literals $\ell_1, \ell_2, \ell_3 : \mathrm{Literal}\,V$.  Each literal is
either a positive or a negative occurrence of some variable.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Literal satisfaction]
\lean{SATtoColor.SatisfiesLiteral}
\leanok
Given a Boolean assignment $\mathrm{assign} : V \to \mathrm{Bool}$, the
function $\lean{SATtoColor.SatisfiesLiteral}$ evaluates a literal: a positive
literal $\mathrm{pos}(v)$ evaluates to $\mathrm{assign}(v)$, and a negative
literal $\mathrm{neg}(v)$ evaluates to $\neg\,\mathrm{assign}(v)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Clause satisfaction]
\lean{SATtoColor.SatisfiesClause}
\leanok
\uses{SATtoColor.Clause, SATtoColor.SatisfiesLiteral}
Under assignment $\mathrm{assign}$, a clause $c$ is satisfied if at least one
of its three literals evaluates to \texttt{true}:
\[
  \mathrm{SatisfiesClause}(\mathrm{assign}, c)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{SatisfiesLiteral}(\mathrm{assign}, c.\ell_1)
  \;\vee\;
  \mathrm{SatisfiesLiteral}(\mathrm{assign}, c.\ell_2)
  \;\vee\;
  \mathrm{SatisfiesLiteral}(\mathrm{assign}, c.\ell_3).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[3-SAT instance]
\lean{SATtoColor.Sat3}
\leanok
\uses{SATtoColor.Clause}
A 3-SAT instance over variable type $V$ is defined as a list of clauses,
i.e.\ $\mathrm{Sat3}(V) := \mathrm{List}(\mathrm{Clause}\,V)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Simultaneous clause satisfaction]
\lean{SATtoColor.SatisfiesSat3}
\leanok
\uses{SATtoColor.Sat3, SATtoColor.SatisfiesClause}
An assignment $\mathrm{assign}$ \emph{satisfies} a 3-SAT instance $f$ if every
clause in the list $f$ is satisfied by $\mathrm{assign}$, i.e.\
$\mathrm{SatisfiesSat3}(\mathrm{assign}, f) = \texttt{true}$ iff
$\forall c \in f,\; \mathrm{SatisfiesClause}(\mathrm{assign}, c) = \texttt{true}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Satisfiability]
\lean{SATtoColor.IsSatisfiable}
\leanok
\uses{SATtoColor.Sat3, SATtoColor.SatisfiesSat3}
A 3-SAT instance $f$ is \emph{satisfiable} if there exists a Boolean
assignment that satisfies it:
\[
  \mathrm{IsSatisfiable}(f)
  \;:=\;
  \exists\,\mathrm{assign}: V \to \mathrm{Bool},\;
  \mathrm{SatisfiesSat3}(\mathrm{assign}, f) = \texttt{true}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Concrete 3-SAT example]
\lean{SATtoColor.SAT3_Example.sat3_inst}
\leanok
\uses{SATtoColor.Sat3}
A specific 3-SAT instance over four Boolean variables $x_0, x_1, x_2, x_3$
($V = \mathrm{Fin}\,4$), consisting of three clauses:
$(x_0 \vee \neg x_1 \vee \neg x_2)$,
$(\neg x_0 \vee x_1 \vee \neg x_2)$, and
$(\neg x_0 \vee \neg x_1 \vee \neg x_3)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Example assignment]
\lean{SATtoColor.SAT3_Example.ex_assign_1}
\leanok
A concrete Boolean assignment for the example instance
$\lean{SATtoColor.SAT3\_Example.sat3\_inst}$, defined as the vector
$[{\tt true},\,{\tt true},\,{\tt false},\,{\tt false}]$ indexed by
$\mathrm{Fin}\,4$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Reduction vertex type]
\lean{SATtoColor.OutputVertex}
\leanok
\uses{SATtoColor.Clause}
The vertex set of the reduction graph is the inductive type
$\mathrm{OutputVertex}(V)$ with three constructors:
\begin{itemize}
  \item $\mathrm{palette}(p)$ for $p : \mathrm{Fin}\,3$ --- the three special
        palette nodes (Base $= 0$, True $= 1$, False $= 2$) forming a triangle
        that fixes color semantics;
  \item $\mathrm{literalNode}(\ell)$ --- one node per literal over $V$
        (positive and negative occurrences are separate nodes);
  \item $\mathrm{clauseGadget}(c, k)$ for $k : \mathrm{Fin}\,6$ --- six
        internal nodes per clause $c$ encoding the OR constraint.
\end{itemize}
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[3-colorability]
\lean{SATtoColor.Is3Colorable}
\leanok
A simple graph $G$ on vertex type $V'$ is \emph{3-colorable} if there exists a
proper graph coloring with colors $\mathrm{Fin}\,3$, i.e.\
$\mathrm{Nonempty}(G.\mathrm{Coloring}(\mathrm{Fin}\,3))$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Reduction edge relation]
\lean{SATtoColor.EdgeRelation}
\leanok
\uses{SATtoColor.OutputVertex, SATtoColor.Sat3}
$\mathrm{EdgeRelation}(f, u, v)$ defines the (undirected) adjacency structure
of the reduction graph.  The edges are:
all pairs of distinct palette nodes;
every literal node to the Base palette node;
$\mathrm{pos}(x)$ to $\mathrm{neg}(x)$ for each variable $x$;
specific pairs of clause gadget nodes within the same clause (encoding two
internal triangles on nodes $\{0,1,2\}$ and $\{3,4,5\}$ plus the bridge
$2$--$3$);
each clause's three literal nodes to gadget nodes $0$, $1$, and $4$
respectively;
and gadget node $5$ of every clause to both the Base and the False palette
nodes.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Reduction graph]
\lean{SATtoColor.ReductionGraph}
\leanok
\uses{SATtoColor.EdgeRelation, SATtoColor.OutputVertex, SATtoColor.Sat3}
Given a 3-SAT instance $f$ over variables $V$, the \emph{reduction graph}
$\mathrm{ReductionGraph}(f)$ is the \texttt{SimpleGraph} on
$\mathrm{OutputVertex}(V)$ whose adjacency relation is the symmetrisation of
$\mathrm{EdgeRelation}(f)$: two distinct vertices are adjacent iff
$\mathrm{EdgeRelation}(f, u, v)$ or $\mathrm{EdgeRelation}(f, v, u)$ holds.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Clause gadget coloring]
\lean{SATtoColor.clauseGadgetColor}
\leanok
Given the Boolean truth values $a, b, c_3$ of the three literals of a clause,
$\mathrm{clauseGadgetColor}(a, b, c_3, k)$ assigns a color in $\mathrm{Fin}\,3$
to gadget node $k \in \{0,\ldots,5\}$.  In particular, node $5$ always receives
color $1$ (True), and the remaining nodes are colored so that all internal
gadget edges receive distinct colors whenever at least one literal is true.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Coloring from satisfying assignment]
\lean{SATtoColor.sat3Coloring}
\leanok
\uses{SATtoColor.OutputVertex, SATtoColor.SatisfiesLiteral, SATtoColor.clauseGadgetColor}
Given a satisfying assignment $\mathrm{assign} : V \to \mathrm{Bool}$, the
function $\mathrm{sat3Coloring}(\mathrm{assign})$ maps every vertex of
$\mathrm{OutputVertex}(V)$ to a color in $\mathrm{Fin}\,3$: palette node $p$
gets color $p$; a positive (resp.\ negative) literal node for variable $v$
gets color $1$ (True) if $\mathrm{assign}(v) = \texttt{true}$ and color $2$
(False) otherwise (resp.\ the reverse); clause gadget node $(c, k)$ gets
$\mathrm{clauseGadgetColor}$ applied to the truth values of $c$'s three
literals.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Literal node color formula]
\lean{SATtoColor.sat3Coloring_litNode}
\leanok
\uses{SATtoColor.SatisfiesLiteral, SATtoColor.sat3Coloring}
\difficulty{3}
For any assignment $\mathrm{assign}$ and literal $\ell$,
\[
  \mathrm{sat3Coloring}(\mathrm{assign},\,\mathrm{literalNode}(\ell))
  \;=\;
  \text{if } \mathrm{SatisfiesLiteral}(\mathrm{assign}, \ell) \text{ then } 1 \text{ else } 2.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Completeness of reduction]
\lean{SATtoColor.SATtoColorCompleteness}
\leanok
\uses{SATtoColor.EdgeRelation, SATtoColor.Is3Colorable, SATtoColor.IsSatisfiable, SATtoColor.OutputVertex, SATtoColor.ReductionGraph, SATtoColor.Sat3, SATtoColor.SatisfiesClause, SATtoColor.SatisfiesLiteral, SATtoColor.clauseGadgetColor, SATtoColor.sat3Coloring, SATtoColor.sat3Coloring_litNode}
\difficulty{6}
If the 3-SAT instance $f$ is satisfiable, then the reduction graph
$\mathrm{ReductionGraph}(f)$ is 3-colorable.  Formally:
\[
  \mathrm{IsSatisfiable}(f) \;\Longrightarrow\;
  \mathrm{Is3Colorable}(\mathrm{ReductionGraph}(f)).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Soundness of reduction]
\lean{SATtoColor.SATtoColorSoundness}
\leanok
\uses{SATtoColor.Clause, SATtoColor.EdgeRelation, SATtoColor.Is3Colorable, SATtoColor.IsSatisfiable, SATtoColor.OutputVertex, SATtoColor.ReductionGraph, SATtoColor.Sat3, SATtoColor.SatisfiesClause, SATtoColor.SatisfiesLiteral, SATtoColor.SatisfiesSat3}
\difficulty{7}
If the reduction graph $\mathrm{ReductionGraph}(f)$ is 3-colorable, then the
3-SAT instance $f$ is satisfiable.  Formally:
\[
  \mathrm{Is3Colorable}(\mathrm{ReductionGraph}(f)) \;\Longrightarrow\;
  \mathrm{IsSatisfiable}(f).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[3-SAT to 3-Coloring reduction]
\lean{SATtoColor.SATtoColorReduction}
\leanok
\uses{SATtoColor.Is3Colorable, SATtoColor.IsSatisfiable, SATtoColor.ReductionGraph, SATtoColor.SATtoColorCompleteness, SATtoColor.SATtoColorSoundness, SATtoColor.Sat3}
\difficulty{1}
A 3-SAT instance $f$ is satisfiable if and only if the reduction graph is
3-colorable:
\[
  \mathrm{IsSatisfiable}(f)
  \;\longleftrightarrow\;
  \mathrm{Is3Colorable}(\mathrm{ReductionGraph}(f)).
\]
This is the conjunction of completeness and soundness of the reduction.
\end{theorem}
